narrative_purpose: Shows the banshee's wing as a real flight instrument: a leathery membrane stiffened by trailing-edge vanes, with a free clawed thumb at the leading edge - the design the chapter argues lets a giant flier shape airflow and fight the low-speed stall.
subject: A single mountain banshee fore-wing spread flat and seen from above as a naturalist study: a long arm-bone runs along the leading edge to a small free clawed thumb at the wrist; behind it a translucent leathery membrane is stretched taut, stiffened by a fan of several large semi-rigid vanes along the trailing edge, faint cyan bioluminescent veins threading through the membrane. A small separate cutaway inset to one side shows the resin-filled vein of a single vane in cross-section, a rigid transparent core within the membrane.
scene: A dark display surface, the wing laid out as if pinned for study, deep haze beyond, generous empty dark space around the wing.
camera: A clean top-down study view of the whole wing, the wing sharp, the inset smaller and set to one side, background soft.
light: Cool clinical glow plus faint bioluminescence within the wing veins and along the vanes; deep indigo shadow.
palette: Void-indigo ground, cool bone-grey on the arm-bone and vanes, pale teal-translucent membrane, faint cyan glow in the veins.
style: Painterly naturalist specimen plate, hand-painted texture, anatomical clarity.
detail_level: Crisp on the arm-bone, clawed thumb, membrane, and trailing-edge vanes plus the cutaway inset; background dissolving into haze.
composition: The spread wing filling the centre with the clawed thumb upper-left and vanes along the lower trailing edge, the cutaway inset lower-right, generous dark margins for callouts, 16:9.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette with bioluminescent key from within the membrane. Same dark glowing-specimen mood as the chapter cover and the 2-6 banshee plates.
